newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-GERMANS TURN OUT IN FORCE TO GREET ULLRICH.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-GERMANS TURN OUT IN FORCE TO GREET ULLRICH.

text.p: Thousands of German fans, including Jan Ullrich's mother Mariana, poured into Colmar and lined the last 30 kms of the Tour de France 17th stage to cheer their new hero on Wednesday.
"It's unbelievable. I thought the whole of Germany was there," Ullrich said after the 218.5-km stage from Fribourg in Switzerland.
It was the first time on the Tour that German fans had outnumbered those from other countries after a strong showing by Danes, Dutch, Italian and Spanish in the Pyrenees and Alps.
There were banners reading "Schliegen greets you Jan Ullrich" or "Jan Ullrich, Tour King, Merdingen fans greet you and your team" and hundreds of German flags along the route.
Ullrich, who lives in the nearby Black Forest village of Merdingen, first came to the notice of the German public when he finished second behind his Danish team mate Bjarne Riis in the 1996 Tour.

This year he has displaced the likes of Boris Becker and Steffi Graf as a national sporting icon after snatching the yellow jersey of overall leader in the Pyrenees and retaining it for a ninth consecutive stage at Colmar.
"It's the first time I've been here," said Ullrich's mother Mariana Kaatz, who brought up her sons on her own in the east German port city of Rostock. "But I was in Paris last year."
Barring a catastrophe, Ullrich will be crowned Tour champion on the Champs Elysees in Paris on Sunday.
The 23-year-old Ullrich looked embarrassed by his mother's public show of emotion when she embraced him as he came off the podium.
Ullrich said: "I'm naturally very happy with the yellow jersey, especially today for my whole family."
